OpenAI, Monochromatic finite sums and products in the positive integers,
September 23, 2026.
https://github.com/openai/math/tree/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/Monochromatic-finite-sums-and-products-in-the-positive-integers-September-23-2026

Target: arbitrary finite coloring of the positive integers; arbitrarily large
finite sets with all nonempty subset sums and products in one common color.
JSP-000168 maps to Erdős #172. Erdős #168 is a DIFFERENT problem.

Formalization environment:
Lean 4.32.2; mathlib 905b95818eb32af7874a58b427f50c1711a5e96c.
The initial environment reuses an already installed pinned mathlib cache.
This is an independent project, and does not modify the Erdős #953 source.

Dependency route:
1. Master scales, harmonic sampling, rough coprimality, weighted linear forms.
2. Correlation test retaining arbitrary multiplicative masks.
3. Prediction: dense models, subgroup cube norms, concatenation, energy Ramsey.
4. Rough progression comparison, local nilmanifold cube laws, joint face lifts.
5. Alignment: finite word plan, conditional mass independent of model complexity.
6. Product-monochromatic chain selection and deduction of the main theorem.

Proof-audit status:
The target and finite-set interfaces have been formalized and compiled.
The full analytic chain is NOT assumed as axioms in Lean and is not yet proved.
The attributed AP-PNT input and its prime-pool consequences are now verified;
the later weighted linear-forms, Prediction and Alignment inputs remain open.
No claim of a completed prize submission is made.
The paper's assertion alone is not evidence of a verified mathematical proof.

Round completed on 2026-10-07:
1. Basic.lean: exact finite and subtype targets, indexed-to-set transfer, m=0,1.
2. Scales.lean: binary-weight domination, product-scale identity, W^w factor
   divisibility, and the own-target integer residue-shift identity.
3. FiniteSums.lean: positive m-term finite-sums patterns from mathlib's additive
   Hindman theorem; compactness of the coloring space gives uniform F(m,r).
   Auxiliary summands may repeat. This matches the input needed for the
   paper's chain-selection argument and does not prove simultaneous products.
4. StrongStatement.lean: the full separated-witness proposition with real
   R>=2 and D>=1; its conditional implication for the original prize target.
5. Compilation and kernel-axiom checks passed. See BUILD-EVIDENCE.txt.

Mathematical review this round:
- The finite target requires arbitrarily large finite sets, not an infinite
  simultaneous sequence. Zero-based indices and Nat zero cause no weakening:
  the indexed interface records positivity and exact cardinality.
- The binary-weight arithmetic behind the master scales is proved in Lean.
- The paper's use of Tao-Ziegler Theorem 1.23 was compared with the primary
  source. Finite subgroups are rank-zero progressions; their dilations do not
  change them, and weighted finite index laws can be approximated by repetition.
  Reference: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1603.07815v4 , Theorem 1.23.
- Read the weighted linear-forms, mask-removal, rough-step comparison,
  local-cube-law, face-lift and conditional-alignment arguments. No definite
  counterexample has been identified. This is a preliminary mathematical
  reading, not a kernel-verified proof of these analytic claims.
- Alignment's probability constant must be independent of the threshold and
  nilsequence model complexity. Prediction's nilpotence step must depend only
  on m. Their quantifiers and order of choices remain explicit review targets.
- OpenAI's Progressions/Nilpotent modules provide some related foundations.
  Their applicability to general GTZ inverse results and this paper's joint
  cube laws is not established by matching names; inspect exact hypotheses.

Completed round on 2026-10-07: chain selection and master arithmetic.
1. Ramsey.lean: arbitrary-uniformity infinite hypergraph Ramsey, successive
   homogeneity by subset cardinality, and a uniform finite interval bound
   obtained by compactness. No unproved Ramsey assumption or numerical bound
   is used. The proof strategy is the standard reservoir induction, also
   used in Bhavik Mehta's Lean 3 inf_ramsey.lean (source linked in the module).
2. Chain.lean: the exact ordered-tail/singleton-pivot structure, pairwise
   disjoint blocks, product and cardinality identities for block unions,
   prescribed-size allocation in positions and in an arbitrary ordered
   finite index set, and the adding-block relation for earlier chain blocks.
3. product_chain_selection is now a fully proved theorem. It follows the
   paper's route: uniform finite-sums bound F; a 2F-element Ramsey-by-size
   set; auxiliary coloring kappa(2a); sizes q_d=2u_d; successive tails of
   size q_d-1 followed by m single pivots. Every nonempty product of the
   block products has one common color. The bound depends only on m,r.
4. MasterScales.lean: zero-based reversed weights 2^(N-1-j), the exact
   product-scale identity, integer divisibility for all bounded adding
   blocks, chain-scale divisibility, and a common power-of-W modulus that
   bounds all subset scales. Every nonempty scale contains W^w.
5. The whole project builds, and the checked results have only the standard
   Lean axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. No sorry/admit/sorryAx
   or axiom/constant/unsafe declarations occur in the proof sources.

Review conclusions of this round:
- The chain ordering is not replaced by whole-block ordering. All tails
  precede all pivots, so earlier blocks lie in the exact adding-block family.
- Repeated auxiliary u_d are allowed; distinct positive final witnesses
  will come from scale separation in the main deduction, not this lemma.
- Natural-number subtraction in the reversed exponents is used only on
  bounded indices when injectivity/order reversal is required.
- Product chain selection does not claim simultaneous additive homogeneity.
- The finite Ramsey bounds are existential, exactly as required by the paper.
- The full asymptotic master-scales lemma is not established merely by its
  proved divisibility component. Prime pools, harmonic laws, roughness and
  the quantitative growth estimates still need proof.

Latest completed round on 2026-10-07: periodic harmonic sampling.
1. HarmonicProgression.lean: affine inverse integral, upper/lower sum-integral
   comparisons, and the sharp 1/A harmonic error for one progression. The
   estimate includes the empty progression and real interval endpoints.
2. ResidueHarmonic.lean: exact enumeration of a residue class in [A,B), using
   natural-number ceilings without an extra rounding error. Every class
   has error at most 1/A. The representative condition a<q is explicit.
3. PeriodicHarmonic.lean: CRT proves exactly phi(W) allowed classes modulo
   W*k when W and k are coprime. The disjoint class partition and summation
   prove the paper's periodic-harmonic estimate with error phi(W)/A.
4. HarmonicSampling.lean: the exact window [X,X^2) of W-units, the normalizer
   Z_X and its error/lower bound. Under X>=2, W>0 and log X>W/X, Z_X>0.
   The normalized weights sum to 1 and define an actual mathlib PMF; its
   support is proved equal to the W-unit window. The residue probabilities
   are proved equal to coefficients of the actual modulo-k pushforward PMF.
5. The paper's bound |k P(Y=a mod k)-1|<=E_X(k) and the whole residue law's
   total-mass error <=E_X(k) are fully proved. The latter is the sum of
   absolute coefficient errors; probability total variation is half of it.

   or axiom/constant/unsafe declarations occur in the proof sources. The

Review conclusions of the harmonic round:
- The periodic estimate retains the original constant phi(W)/A. In the
  proof, the upper bound separates the first progression term and the
  lower bound controls the missing initial integral. This avoids an extra
  factor from a coarse two-endpoint discrepancy argument.
- Half-open intervals and nonintegral endpoints are exact; these will be
  needed at X/k and X^2/k in the dilation identity.
- Positivity of Z_X is proved from the same growth condition as the paper,
  not imposed as an unverified axiom. PMF takes its proved positivity as a
  parameter; harmonicNormalizer_pos supplies that parameter under the
  paper's stated hypotheses.
- The factor k+1 in E_X(k) includes both class-mass and normalizer errors.
- The raw sample PMF is on positive natural numbers. Its extension to Z
  and signed translation/dilation laws are still to be constructed.
- This round proves the residue/normalization part of the sampling lemma,
  not its translation, dilation or asymptotic conclusions.

Latest completed round on 2026-10-07: finite masses and harmonic dilation.
1. FiniteMass.lean defines the sum of absolute coefficients, finite signed
   expectation and L1 distance. Injective pushforward preserves the distance;
   bounded test functions transmit an error with precisely their sup bound.
2. HarmonicMass.lean proves interval splitting and exact overlap cancellation.
   The denominator Z is fixed throughout. A comparison interval is not
   silently normalized when the endpoints change.
3. HarmonicDilation.lean proves eta_k=k*1_{k|n}*mu_X by an injective change
   of variables. The exact L1 difference consists of the two boundary
   harmonic sums on [X/k,X) and [X^2/k,X^2), divided by the original Z_X.
4. The full paper bound is proved with the original constants:
   [2 log k + (W k/X)(1+1/X)] / [log X-W/X], under X>=2, W>0,
   1<=k<=X, gcd(W,k)=1 and log X>W/X. The k=1 case is included.
   The total mass of eta_k differs from 1 by at most E_X(k), proved
   independently from the residue probability of zero modulo k.
5. The natural-number masses are extended to integers. The integer
   comparison is exactly k*1_{k|z}*mu_X(z), including negative z, and
   integer dilation has the same L1 distance and error. The integer raw
   mass is nonnegative, has total mass 1 and is proved coefficientwise
   equal to the actual pushed-forward mathlib PMF on integers.
6. Full build and all 37 selected kernel dependency reports passed, with
   only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Proof-source scans found
   no sorry/admit/sorryAx or axiom/constant/unsafe declarations. The
   verification manifest includes all three new modules and fresh hashes.

Review conclusions of the dilation round:
- eta_k is an unnormalized positive comparison weight. No proof assumes
  its mass is exactly 1; its mass error is retained for product comparisons.
- The L1 norm is the sum of absolute masses, not the Finsupp sup norm and
  not probability total variation (which is half the L1 distance).
- The overlap order X/k<=X<=X^2/k<=X^2 is proved from 1<=k<=X.
- Boundary endpoint equality is handled separately, so k=1 needs no
  appeal to a strict-interval harmonic estimate.
- The proofs agree with 03_arithmetic.tex equations harmonic-dilation
  and harmonic-residue-error at the pinned OpenAI commit. No mathematical
  gap was identified in this component. This does not validate the later
  analytic principles or their asymptotic conclusions.

Latest completed round on 2026-10-07: harmonic translation.
1. FiniteMass.lean proves that equal total masses make the L1 distance
   twice a pointwise deficit, and that translations by h and -h have
   exactly the same distance from the original integer mass.
2. HarmonicTranslation.lean identifies the deficit of the positive shift
   H as the original raw mass below X+H. Coprimality is preserved using
   W|H; on the overlap, the reciprocal weight of n-H is at least that of n.
3. The complete-period count is proved for any starting integer X:
   [X,X+W*t) contains precisely t*phi(W) units modulo W. Thus when W|H,
   the number of units in [X,X+H) equals unitDensity(W)*H.
4. The lower-boundary mass is at most unitDensity(W)*H/(X*Z_X), for all
   H, even if X+H exceeds X^2. Comparing denominators proves the original
   linear bound 2H/[X*(log X-W/X)]. The distance also is at most 2.
5. Natural positive shifts commute with the integer inclusion, preserving
   L1 distance. Arbitrary signed shifts reduce exactly to h.natAbs.
   The resulting integer theorem proves the paper's full bound
   min(2,2*|h|/[X*(log X-W/X)]) whenever X>=2, W>0, log X>W/X and W|h.

Review conclusions of the translation round:
- The exact deficit identity, rather than a coarse overlap estimate,
  preserves the paper's factor 2 and has no extra endpoint-counting loss.
- The boundary coefficient is a filter of the ORIGINAL normalized law.
  No comparison interval is assigned a new normalizing denominator.
- Complete periods have integer endpoints and length divisible by W.
  The proof does not apply the exact counting assertion to arbitrary lengths.
- All shifts, including H=0, negative h and shifts larger than the window,
  are covered. Bounding the truncated boundary mass by the larger complete
  period interval removes the need for a separate large-H logarithm argument.
- All finite numerical inequalities of the harmonic sampling lemma are
  now proved. Its asymptotic little-o assertions are still unproved.
- No mathematical gap was identified in this component. This is not a

Latest completed round on 2026-10-07: finite block-product sampling.
1. FiniteMixture.lean proves linear total mass, scalar variation, the
   variation triangle inequality and averaging of L1 errors over finite
   probability coefficients. Comparison components need not have mass one.
   A separate lemma averages their total-mass errors.
2. FiniteProbability.lean constructs actual PMFs from finite nonnegative
   real masses of total one. Coefficients are proved equal under arbitrary
   pushforward and PMF.bind, including maps that are not injective.
3. ProductLaw.lean constructs the actual law of sigma*Y using an independent
   tail law rho and a harmonic pivot. Its PMF coefficients equal productMass.
   The comparison coefficients are exactly mu_X(n)*divisorMask(rho,n),
   where divisorMask is sum_k rho(k)*k*1_{k|n}. They are nonnegative, but
   are not asserted to have total mass exactly one.
4. For rho supported on positive W-units at most K and K<=X, the full
   quantitative comparison is bounded by dilationError(X,W,K). Both the
   logarithmic and arithmetic terms are proved monotone in k. The total
   mass of the comparison differs from one by at most residueError(X,W,K),
   independently of the K<=X restriction.
5. TailProducts.lean recursively constructs the independent harmonic tail
   law, starting with the deterministic empty product one. PMF recursion
   is proved equal to independent bind/map sampling, not just an abstract
   family of finite weights. From the raw supports, its support is proved
   positive, coprime to W and bounded by the product of squared cutoffs.
   The single-block finite comparison and mass errors follow with all
   tail support hypotheses discharged.

Review conclusions of the product round:
- The tail is independent of the pivot by the explicit PMF bind/map
  construction, and all finite mixtures correspond to those actual PMFs.
- Divisor conditioning and sampling of a multiplied argument remain
  distinct. Their comparison uses the exact unnormalized eta_k weights.
- The empty tail is permitted and has product one. Arbitrary lists of
  cutoffs permit repeated cutoff values; each occurrence is an independent
  draw, as required for different raw variables with the same size.
- No support positivity, coprimality or tail bound is assumed for a
  genuine harmonic tail; all three are derived from its raw samples.
- This round proves the single-block finite quantitative comparison.
  It does not prove the little-o conclusion, the independence/reindexing
  identity for a family of disjoint blocks, or the joint tensor error.
- No mathematical gap was identified in this component. Prediction,
  Alignment and the later analytic inputs remain unverified in Lean.

Latest completed round on 2026-10-07: tensor errors and independent joint products.
1. FiniteTensor.lean constructs finite signed tensor masses, proving that
   their total masses and variations multiply. The binary telescope is
   ||mu*nu-mu'*nu'||_1 <= ||mu-mu'||_1 ||nu||_1
                              + ||mu'||_1 ||nu-nu'||_1.
   Arbitrary finite list tensors have a recursive telescope that retains
   all original-tail and comparison-prefix variation factors.
2. For probability original factors and nonnegative comparison factors of
   mass at most M, each of error at most E, the joint error is at most
   E * sum_{j<n} M^j. Comparison factors are not silently normalized.
   The proof includes zero factors and empty families.
3. TensorProbability.lean proves that the actual independent PMF pair has
   product coefficients, that it equals the corresponding finite tensor,
   and that applying separate functions to independent coordinates commutes
   with their tensor law. List PMFs are proved recursively equal to actual
   independent draws through bind/map and start with the deterministic
   empty list. Only total-one nonnegative originals are converted to PMFs.
4. IntegerProductLaw.lean transports the single-block product law and
   comparison to integers. The comparison is exactly the integer raw mass
   times E[sigma*1_{sigma|z}] for every z, including negative z. Its actual
   product PMF, complete L1 bound and total-mass error are identified.
5. JointProductLaw.lean constructs actual independent harmonic block-product
   PMFs. Each block's nonnegativity, total one, comparison coefficients,
   L1 error and mass error come from the already verified tail/pivot laws.
   The comparison coefficients recursively multiply mu_i(y_i)*nu_B(y_i).
   Joint errors are bounded by E * sum_{j<n} M^j when each dilation error
   is <=E and each residue mass error is <=M-1. Natural and integer joint
   errors agree under the explicitly injective coordinate inclusion.

Review conclusions of the joint round:
- The general telescope uses variation factors, not an assumption that
  every comparison is a probability. For nonnegative factors these
  variations equal their actual masses, so the paper's 1+o(1) factors
  remain present and can be bounded by a fixed M at the asymptotic stage.
- The joint laws are actual independent products of harmonic blocks;
  comparison weights are positive finite masses with their mass errors.
- Separate-coordinate PMF mapping is proved, but the raw-index permutation
  that identifies a globally indexed independent sample with the disjoint
  Chain blocks has not yet been formalized. It is not assumed as an axiom.
- List integer inclusion uses explicitly typed natural arguments. This
  avoids an unintended lifted coercion of an entire list; injectivity and
  PMF coefficients of the intended coordinate map are proved exactly.
- The finite tensor and independent-block error transfer is complete.
  Little-o conclusions and growth hypotheses of the master scales remain
  unproved. No mathematical gap or unavoidable blocker was established.

Completed round on 2026-10-07: global coordinate and chain-block laws.
1. FiniteCoordinates.lean defines finite dependent coordinate masses with
   exact product coefficients and actual normalized PMFs. Coordinate
   reindexing, restriction to an injective index selection, sigma grouping
   and separate-coordinate pushforwards are proved. Unused coordinates
   are integrated out using their total-one masses. Disjoint block
   statistics therefore have their exact independent product law.
2. CoordinateLists.lean identifies coordinate samples listed by List.ofFn
   with the earlier recursive tensorList mass. Tensor pushforwards under
   separate maps and arbitrary two-coordinate statistics are proved as
   finite signed-mass equalities, without normalization assumptions.
3. CoordinateProducts.lean identifies the product of raw harmonic
   coordinates with the verified recursive tailMass, for any prescribed
   finite enumeration. The equality itself assumes no probability bounds.
4. GlobalChainLaw.lean proves a bijection between a chain block and its
   tail plus singleton pivot, uses the tail's increasing enumeration, and
   identifies its coordinate product with blockOriginal. Block coordinates
   embed injectively in the global Fin N sample by blocks_disjoint.
   The actual global product PMF, after selecting chain blocks and taking
   their products, equals jointProductPMF. The natural and integer mass
   identities and integer PMF coefficients are also proved.
5. The joint E * sum_{j<m} M^j error bounds now apply to products extracted
   from that global sample, retaining the comparison-mass factors. These
   statements explicitly require valid block cutoffs, positive original
   normalizers and the finite component bounds; they do not claim that
   the asymptotic master scales already meet those hypotheses.

Completed round on 2026-10-07: power growth and sampling asymptotics.
1. PowerGrowth.lean states power domination as Q^n=o(F) for every fixed
   natural n and proves polynomial-majorant error transfer. If |e| is
   bounded by A*Q^p/F and 1<=V<=Q eventually, then e=o(V^-C) for every
   fixed natural C. Fixed polynomial losses and constants are absorbed.
   The rates extend to every real C using natural ceilings and rpow.
   Domination transfers to auxiliary budgets bounded by a fixed power.
2. SamplingMajorants.lean derives eventual-use bounds from the previously
   proved sharp formulas. For X>=4, 2W<=X, Q>=2 and W,K,H<=Q, the bounds
   are residueError<=4Q^2/X, translationError<=4Q/X, and
   dilationError<=8Q^2/log X (with K>=1). The errors are nonnegative and
   log X-W/X is bounded below by (log X)/2 and by 1/2.
3. SamplingAsymptotics.lean derives all three inverse-power rates from
   exactly the paper's separate X and log-X domination conditions.
   Growth also implies X>=4, 2W<=X and K<=X eventually, hence the finite
   sampling hypotheses and positivity of the actual normalizer when
   W>0. No small-error assumption replaces the required growth hypothesis.
4. UniformSampling.lean applies those cap-dependent rates to actual
   varying admissible residues/moduli, signed W-multiple translations and
   integer dilations. The same rates are independent of the choice
   k<=K or |h|<=H. It also proves polynomially bounded real-test transfer.
5. NormedExpectation.lean defines finite mass expectations in a real
   normed space, proves the normed L1 difference bound and all inverse
   real-power error rates for polynomially bounded tests. This includes
   complex-valued tests; comparisons are not assumed normalized.
6. CutoffGrowth.lean formalizes the actual explicit dyadic choice
   X(w)=2^ceil(w*R(w)^w/log 2), proves log X>=w*R^w and proves that this
   logarithm dominates every fixed power of R when R>=1 eventually.
   Auxiliary budgets bounded by R^d for fixed d inherit domination and
   all three sampling rates. This is a proved cutoff construction, not
   an assumption about the desired error. Prime pools and the remaining
   smooth/gap master parameters are not yet constructed.

Completed round on 2026-10-07: uniform intervals and joint sampling rates.
1. UniformFiniteMass.lean constructs the actual uniform PMF on any
   nonempty finite set. Flat-mass pushforwards count fibers; injective
   images preserve uniformity. Equal-size supports have exact L1 distance
   twice the exposed cardinality times the common coefficient.
2. IntervalResidueCount.lean proves, over both Q and R, that every residue
   count in [A,A+T) differs from T/k by at most one, for arbitrary signed
   A and positive k. The proof uses the integer interval/modulus counting
   identity and ceiling inequalities, without numerical approximation.
3. UniformIntervals.lean identifies the genuine interval and residue
   PMFs. It derives a location-independent residue L1 bound k/T and hence
   the paper's bound 2k/T. The interval must have positive integer length.
4. UniformIntervalTranslation.lean proves the actual shifted PMF identity
   and exact distance 2*min(1,|u|/T), for every integer u and positive T.
   The signed reduction and disjoint case |u|>=T are included.
5. ProbabilityTensorBounds.lean proves the sum of coordinate errors when
   both tensor factors are probability laws. This specialization does not
   replace the mass-factor bounds for unnormalized harmonic comparisons.
6. ConditionalSampling.lean proves actual PMF bind equals its finite
   probability mixture. Errors uniform in any finite outside-variable
   law survive unconditioning. The interval location, positive length,
   and translation may depend on those variables. Residue and translation
   applications, including the actual conditional residue PMF, are proved.
7. UniformIntervalAsymptotics.lean derives eventual length positivity and
   all inverse-power rates from domination of powers of 2+K+H+V by T.
   Moduli k<=K and signed shifts |u|<=H may vary with the parameter. The
   location is arbitrary. Existing real-exponent and bounded-test transfer
   theorems apply to these rates.
8. ProductSamplingAsymptotics.lean completes the single-block asymptotic
   product-law conclusion from logarithmic cutoff domination. Tail
   support bounds, positivity and normalization are derived from valid
   independent harmonic tail cutoffs. The positive divisor-mask comparison
   remains unnormalized; its mass-minus-one also has all inverse-power
   rates. The result is transported exactly to integer-valued laws.
9. JointSamplingAsymptotics.lean proves that a fixed number of varying
   components with inverse-power L1 rates has the same joint rates.
   The comparison masses are bounded by two eventually using their actual
   L1 distance from the total-one originals. The geometric tensor factors
   are retained until that bound is proved. The paper's fixed-family
   natural and integer block product conclusions follow, as does the
   rate for products extracted from the global raw sample of a fixed chain.

Prime-pool and AP-PNT round, 2026-10-07:
1. PrimePool.lean constructs actual finite prime pools and normalized
   1/p laws, proves the maximum-atom cap 1/(P^- H), and derives arbitrary
   harmonic mass on a union of complete dyadic intervals from divergence
   of the prime reciprocal sum. This does not by itself imply residues
   are equidistributed.
2. SmoothAbsorption.lean uses the actual primorial(w), absorbs every fixed
